title: Read Replicas
subtitle: Scaling read-heavy workloads while solving replication lag anomalies: Read-Your-Writes, Monotonic Reads, and LSN pinning.
keyTakeaways: Read replicas scale read throughput horizontally, but every replica still processes 100% of the write stream: so read replicas do NOT scale write capacity.
Asynchronous replication lag causes users to miss data they just submitted unless Read-Your-Own-Writes consistency is enforced.
Tracking the Log Sequence Number (LSN) or GTID per user session allows intelligent routing between replicas and the primary.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: In systems with a 90:10 read-to-write ratio, offloading `SELECT` queries to read replicas dramatically reduces CPU and I/O pressure on the primary. However, because replicas apply WAL records asynchronously (typically 5ms to 500ms behind), naive round-robin load balancing across replicas introduces jarring user-experience bugs.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: Read replicas scale read throughput horizontally, but every replica still processes 100% of the write stream: so read replicas do NOT scale write capacity.
**Problem Space & Invariants**: Asynchronous replication lag causes users to miss data they just submitted unless Read-Your-Own-Writes consistency is enforced.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Read Replicas:
bullets: **Time-Window Primary Pinning (e.g., 5s after write)**: Provides trivial to implement with redis or an http cookie; requires no db-specific lsn queries. Best suited for Standard web applications, CRUD APIs, and e-commerce user profiles.

**LSN / GTID Causal Watermark Routing**: Provides mathematically guarantees read-your-writes and monotonic reads even during replication lag spikes. Best suited for Collaborative SaaS tools, financial dashboards, and globally distributed read replicas.
Read-Your-Writes Violation: A user posts a comment, refreshes the page, and their comment disappears because the read hit a lagging replica.
Non-Monotonic Reads (Time Travel): A user refreshes twice; the first request hits Replica 1 (lag 5ms, shows new message) and the second hits Replica 2 (lag 300ms, message vanishes).
Write-Window Sticky Routing: Store a short-lived key in Redis (`user_wrote:{id}`, TTL = 5s) on any mutation; route that user's reads to Primary while the key exists.

LSN / GTID Causal Tokens: Return the primary's commit Log Sequence Number (Postgres `pg_current_wal_lsn()`) or MySQL `GTID` to the client; replicas wait or reject until their replay position reaches that LSN.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Read Replicas across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Standard web applications, CRUD APIs, and e-commerce user profiles, suited for environments requiring Trivial to implement with Redis or an HTTP cookie; requires no DB-specific LSN queries.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Collaborative SaaS tools, financial dashboards, and globally distributed read replicas, where Mathematically guarantees Read-Your-Writes and Monotonic Reads even during replication lag spikes.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: To preserve strong user-perceived consistency without routing all reads back to the primary, production systems combine session affinity with write-tracking watermarks. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Read Replicas introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: routes all reads from active writers to primary; breaks if replication lag spikes beyond 5s.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: requires proxy/driver support (e.g., proxysql, pgpool, or custom middleware) to track lsns.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Read Replicas:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Tracking the Log Sequence Number (LSN) or GTID per user session allows intelligent routing between replicas and the primary.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Whenever you add Read Replicas to your architecture diagram, proactively tell the interviewer how you will handle 'Read-Your-Own-Writes' for the user who just mutated state: this immediately signals senior production experience.
